newsitem.title: USA: Alaska gov't says Japan firm plans fish project.
newsitem.headline: Alaska gov't says Japan firm plans fish project.

text.p: A Japanese company has promised to experiment next year with the processing of Alaska arrowtooth flounder, a fish that until now has found no market, Alaska Governor Tony Knowles said on Monday.
The Marubeni Corp. plans to buy up to one million pounds of the fish, one of the most plentiful species in the Gulf of Alaska and Bering Sea, Knowles said.
The plan for arrowtooth flounder came after a five-day trade mission to Japan and South Korea, the governor said in a news conference held upon his return to Alaska.
Arrowtooth flounder has been nearly useless as a commercial product because of an enzyme that turns the fish to "mush" when cooked, Knowles said.
"Right now, the fish is a trash fish," Knowles said. "It's a predator and a competitor for other species."
But Marubeni hopes to develop a technology to counteract the enzyme, the governor said.
The trade mission, which included several private-sector representatives, helped improve relations with buyers of Alaska fish and other products, Knowles said.
"We really, I think, set a whole new approach for dealing with our customers, and the reason why I say that is because that's what they told us," he said.
The trade mission included representatives from Alaska's oil, gas and coal producers, miners, environmental-cleanup services and tourism operators.
